title: REST vs gRPC vs GraphQL
description: Compare REST, gRPC, and GraphQL protocols for service communication.

data.text: Choosing the right communication protocol is critical for microservices. REST, gRPC, and GraphQL each have distinct strengths. This lesson compares them across performance, code generation, and use cases.

terms.definition: An architectural style using HTTP verbs and resources.
A high-performance RPC framework using HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers.
A query language for APIs that lets clients request exactly the data they need.
A language-neutral mechanism for serializing structured data used by gRPC.

items: REST: Public APIs, simple CRUD, browser clients
gRPC: Internal service-to-service, high performance, streaming
GraphQL: Complex data requirements, mobile clients, aggregating data

data.text: gRPC is typically 5-10x faster than REST for internal communication due to HTTP/2 multiplexing and Protocol Buffers serialization. GraphQL can be slower due to query parsing but reduces over-fetching.
gRPC uses Protocol Buffers to generate client and server code in multiple languages. REST and GraphQL can use OpenAPI and GraphQL schema respectively, but code generation is optional.

data.title: Exercise: Choose a Protocol
data.description: For each scenario, choose REST, gRPC, or GraphQL and justify your choice.
steps: Public API for a mobile app
Internal communication between inventory and order services
Dashboard that needs data from 5 different services
data.expectedOutcome: A table with protocol choices and justifications

items.question: Is gRPC better than REST?
items.answer: For internal service-to-service communication, yes. For public APIs, REST is simpler and more widely supported.

items.question: Can I use GraphQL with microservices?
items.answer: Yes, GraphQL can act as an API gateway that aggregates data from multiple services.

items.question: Does gRPC work in browsers?
items.answer: Not directly. You need a proxy like Envoy or grpc-web to use gRPC from browsers.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: REST for public APIs, gRPC for internal, GraphQL for flexible queries
gRPC is fastest but requires code generation
Choose based on client type, performance needs, and data requirements
data.takeaway: Match the protocol to the use case: REST for public, gRPC for internal, GraphQL for flexible data.
